name: Nucleoid (Chromosomal DNA)
description: The irregularly shaped region within the cell where the ~4.6 million base pair circular chromosome is localized. UV radiation causes thymine dimers and double-strand breaks along this DNA.

name: Ribosomes
description: Complex molecular machines (70S in bacteria) that translate mRNA into proteins. During the SOS response, ribosomes translate upregulated repair genes.

name: GamGFP (DSB Sensor)
description: A fusion of bacteriophage Mu Gam protein and Green Fluorescent Protein. Gam binds to DNA double-strand break ends, forming bright green fluorescent foci that mark DSB locations in real time.

reference.title: Shee, C., Cox, B. D., Gu, F., Luengas, E. M., Joshi, M. C., Chiu, L. Y., Magnan, D., Rosenberg, S. M., Frisch, R. L., & Hastings, P. J. (2013). Engineered proteins detect spontaneous DNA breakage in human and bacterial cells. eLife, 2, e01222.

name: RecA Filaments
description: RecA protein polymerizes on single-stranded DNA at DSB sites, forming nucleoprotein filaments. These filaments catalyze homologous recombination for repair and also trigger the SOS response by stimulating LexA auto-cleavage.

reference.title: Shee, C., Cox, B. D., Gu, F., Luengas, E. M., Joshi, M. C., Chiu, L. Y., Magnan, D., Rosenberg, S. M., Frisch, R. L., & Hastings, P. J. (2013). Engineered proteins detect spontaneous DNA breakage in human and bacterial cells. eLife, 2, e01222.

name: LexA Repressor
description: LexA is a transcriptional repressor that keeps SOS response genes silenced under normal conditions. When RecA filaments form at DSBs, they stimulate LexA to auto-cleavage, derepressing ~40 SOS genes including DNA repair enzymes.

name: RecBCD Enzyme
description: A bacterial helicase-nuclease that processes broken DNA ends during homologous recombination repair. GamGFP competes with RecBCD by capping DNA ends first.

reference.title: Shee, C., Cox, B. D., Gu, F., Luengas, E. M., Joshi, M. C., Chiu, L. Y., Magnan, D., Rosenberg, S. M., Frisch, R. L., & Hastings, P. J. (2013). Engineered proteins detect spontaneous DNA breakage in human and bacterial cells. eLife, 2, e01222.

name: Double-Strand Break (DSB)
description: A severe form of DNA damage where both strands of the double helix are severed. UV radiation and environmental toxins can induce DSBs directly or indirectly via replication fork collapse.

reference.title: Shee, C., Cox, B. D., Gu, F., Luengas, E. M., Joshi, M. C., Chiu, L. Y., Magnan, D., Rosenberg, S. M., Frisch, R. L., & Hastings, P. J. (2013). Engineered proteins detect spontaneous DNA breakage in human and bacterial cells. eLife, 2, e01222.

name: DNA Polymerase IV (DinB)
description: An error-prone DNA polymerase upregulated during the SOS response. It can bypass lesions in DNA that stall normal replication, but its low fidelity often introduces mutations (Stress-Induced Mutagenesis).

reference.title: Shee, C., Gibson, J. L., Darrow, M. C., Gonzalez, C., & Rosenberg, S. M. (2011). Impact of a stress-inducible switch to mutagenic repair of DNA breaks on mutation in Escherichia coli. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 108(33), 13659-13664.

name: Genetic Mutation
description: A permanent alteration in the DNA sequence. Under high stress, E. coli employs error-prone repair mechanisms (like Pol IV), increasing the mutation rate to potentially acquire traits that help it survive the stress.

reference.title: Shee, C., Gibson, J. L., Darrow, M. C., Gonzalez, C., & Rosenberg, S. M. (2011). Impact of a stress-inducible switch to mutagenic repair of DNA breaks on mutation in Escherichia coli. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 108(33), 13659-13664.

name: Plasmid DNA
description: Small, extra-chromosomal circular DNA molecules used to express reporter constructs like GamGFP and TetR-mCherry in the Shee Lab's experimental system.

reference.title: Shee, C., Cox, B. D., Gu, F., Luengas, E. M., Joshi, M. C., Chiu, L. Y., Magnan, D., Rosenberg, S. M., Frisch, R. L., & Hastings, P. J. (2013). Engineered proteins detect spontaneous DNA breakage in human and bacterial cells. eLife, 2, e01222.

name: Thymine Dimers (UV Damage)
description: Covalent linkages between adjacent thymine bases caused by ultraviolet (UV) radiation. Dimers distort the DNA double helix, stalling DNA replication and transcription until repaired by Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER).

reference.title: Sancar, A. (1996). Mechanisms of DNA excision repair. Science, 272(5264), 995-1001.

name: UvrABC Excinuclease Complex
description: The multi-subunit enzyme complex (UvrA, UvrB, UvrC) that performs Nucleotide Excision Repair (NER). UvrAB scans the DNA for bulky helix-distorting lesions like thymine dimers, and UvrC cleaves single-stranded cuts on both sides of the damage to excise the oligonucleotide.

reference.title: Sancar, A. (1996). Mechanisms of DNA excision repair. Science, 272(5264), 995-1001.

name: Oxidative DNA Damage (8-oxoG)
description: Lesions such as 8-oxoguanine and apurinic sites caused by reactive oxygen species (ROS) from H₂O₂ exposure. If unrepaired, 8-oxoG mispairs with adenine during replication, leading to GC → TA transversion mutations.

reference.title: David, S. S., O'Shea, V. L., & Kundu, S. (2007). Base excision repair of oxidative DNA damage. Nature, 447(7147), 941-950.

name: DNA Glycosylase (Fpg / MutM)
description: A Base Excision Repair (BER) enzyme that recognizes and flips out oxidized bases like 8-oxoguanine, cleaving the N-glycosidic bond to initiate BER repair and restore genetic integrity.

reference.title: David, S. S., O'Shea, V. L., & Kundu, S. (2007). Base excision repair of oxidative DNA damage. Nature, 447(7147), 941-950.

name: Capsule
description: The outermost protective layer of the E. coli bacterium.

name: Cell Wall
description: A rigid layer of peptidoglycan that gives the bacterium its shape.

name: Plasma Membrane
description: A phospholipid bilayer controlling transport in and out of the cell.

name: Flagella
description: Helical appendages used for cellular locomotion.

name: Pili / Fimbriae
description: Fine hair-like appendages on the cell surface used for attachment.
